question.text: In a 'core-satellite' portfolio structure, the core (typically 70% to 80%) is generally:

answer.text: All satellite, with no stable anchor

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook describes the core as generally passive, lower-turnover, lower-cost, and long-term, anchoring the portfolio. Satellites are smaller active or tactical allocations around that core. The Trap: Treating the core as active and high-turnover inverts the structure and increases cost drag. Note: Per NISM-XXI-B workbook (p.319 and p.320).
